'''Vladimir Dmitrievich Shiltsev''' ({{langx|ru|Владимир Дми́триевич Шильцев}}; born March 14, 1965) is a Russian-American accelerator [[physicist]], professor at [[Northern Illinois University|NIU]], in 1996-2024 - the Distinguished Scientist at [[Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Shiltsev|first=Vladimir|date=2020-04-01|title=Particle beams behind physics discoveries|journal=Physics Today|volume=73|issue=4|pages=32–39|doi=10.1063/PT.3.4452|bibcode=2020PhT....73d..32S|osti=1632201 |s2cid=216325318|issn=0031-9228|doi-access=free}}</ref> He is best known for his works on particle colliders, invention of electron lenses, leadership in operation of the [[Tevatron]] Collider Run II, and numerous contributions to [[accelerator physics]] and accelerator technology. Shiltsev led the Tevatron collider department and the Fermilab Accelerator Physics Center from 2001 to 2018 and was chair of the American Physical Society's Division of Physics of Beams in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-01-27|title=Anna Grassellino, Vladimir Shiltsev elected to APS Division of Physics of Beams executive committee|url=https://news.fnal.gov/2016/01/grassellino-shiltsev-aps-dpb/ |website=News|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Early life, education and career ==
Shiltsev was born on March 14, 1965, in [[Ivanovka, Kyrgyzstan|Ivanovka]], [[Kirghiz Soviet Socialist Republic|Kirgiz]] SSR, and spent his early years in [[Osinniki]], [[Russia]]. After finishing Physics and [[Specialized Educational Scientific Center|Math School]] in [[Novosibirsk]], [[Russia]], he entered the Physics Department of [[Novosibirsk State University]], from which he graduated summa cum laude in 1988. Shiltsev received his PhD and Dr.Sci. (Habilitation) in accelerator and beam physics from the [[Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics]] (Novosibirsk, Russia) in 1994 and 2017, respectively, and worked at leading accelerator laboratories in Novosibirsk and [[Protvino]], Russia, the [[Superconducting Super Collider]] (SSC) Laboratory in Texas and DESY, before joining [[Fermilab]] as a [[Robert R. Wilson|Robert R. Wilson]] Fellow in 1996.<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.fnal.gov/pub/forphysicists/fellowships/robert_wilson/past.html|title= Past Wilson Fellows|website=www.fnal.gov|access-date=2022-03-20}}</ref> There he initiated and led the project of beam-beam compensation using the Tevatron electron lenses. In 2001 he became Head of the [[Tevatron]] Department<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://cds.cern.ch/record/1379203?ln=en|title= Passing the Baton|website=www.cern.ch|access-date=2022-03-20}}</ref> and one of the leaders of the Collider Run II team at what was then the world's highest-energy particle accelerator.<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.fnal.gov/pub/today/archive/archive_2014/today14-08-20.html|title= The Tevatron Experience|website=www.fnal.gov|access-date=2022-03-20}}</ref>
In 2007–2018 he served as the inaugural Director of the Fermilab Accelerator Physics Center.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Shiltsev|first=Vladimir|date=2018-09-01|title=Accelerator Physics Center at Fermilab: History and Accomplishments (2007-2018)|doi=10.2172/1480101|osti=1480101|s2cid=125471458|url=https://www.osti.gov/biblio/1480101|language=English}}</ref>
In 2026 he joined [[Subcritical Systems, Inc.]] to develop a high-power superconducting proton linear accelerator for the Energy Amplifier — an accelerator-driven subcritical reactor for clean energy generation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://subcritical.com/|title=Subcritical Systems, Inc.|website=subcritical.com|access-date=2026-03-16}}</ref>

== Research ==
Shiltsev's research interests include modern and future colliders,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shiltsev|first1=V.|last2=Zimmermann|first2=F.|date=2021-03-03|title=Modern and future colliders|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/RevModPhys.93.015006|journal=Reviews of Modern Physics|volume=93|issue=1|article-number=015006|doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.93.015006|arxiv=2003.09084|bibcode=2021RvMP...93a5006S|s2cid=214605600}}</ref> with significant contributions to beam physics, space-charge and beam-beam effects and their compensation, particle collimation and beam emittance control; design of large hadron colliders, linear <nowiki>''</nowiki>e+e-<nowiki>''</nowiki> colliders and muon colliders. He authored five books including <nowiki>''</nowiki>Electron Lenses for Super-Colliders<nowiki>''</nowiki> (Springer, 2016<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Shiltsev|first=Vladimir D.|date=2016|title=Electron Lenses for Super-Colliders|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4939-3317-4|journal=Particle Acceleration and Detection|language=en-gb|doi=10.1007/978-1-4939-3317-4|bibcode=2016elsc.book.....S |isbn=978-1-4939-3315-0|issn=1611-1052|url-access=subscription}}</ref> ) and <nowiki>''</nowiki>Accelerator Physics at the Tevatron Collider<nowiki>''</nowiki> (Springer, 2014, with V.Lebedev<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2014|editor-last=Lebedev|editor-first=Valery|editor2-last=Shiltsev|editor2-first=Vladimir|title=Accelerator Physics at the Tevatron Collider|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4939-0885-1|journal=Particle Acceleration and Detection|language=en-gb|doi=10.1007/978-1-4939-0885-1|bibcode=2014aptc.book.....L |isbn=978-1-4939-0884-4|issn=1611-1052|url-access=subscription}}</ref> ), and more than 400 publications. Shiltsev is listed among Top-3 Authors in Fundamental Physics after 2010 (for the INSPIRE database, ''PaperRank''=517.1<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Strumia|first1=Alessandro|last2=Torre|first2=Riccardo|date=May 2019|title=Biblioranking fundamental physics|arxiv=1803.10713|journal=Journal of Informetrics|volume=13|issue=2|pages=515–539|doi=10.1016/j.joi.2019.01.011|s2cid=4374527}}</ref>).

His major research accomplishments include the original idea and pioneering development of electron lenses (1997) – now in use for  beam-beam compensation, halo collimation, Landau damping and space-charge compensation;<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shiltsev|first1=V.|last2=Danilov|first2=V.|last3=Finley|first3=D.|last4=Sery|first4=A.|date=1999-07-28|title=Considerations on compensation of beam-beam effects in the Tevatron with electron beams|journal=Physical Review Special Topics: Accelerators and Beams|volume=2|issue=7|article-number=071001|doi=10.1103/PhysRevSTAB.2.071001|bibcode=1999PhRvS...2g1001S|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shiltsev|first1=V.|last2=Alexahin|first2=Y.|last3=Bishofberger|first3=K.|last4=Kamerdzhiev|first4=V.|last5=Kuznetsov|first5=G.|last6=Zhang|first6=X.-L.|date=2007-12-11|title=Experimental Demonstration of Colliding-Beam-Lifetime Improvement by Electron Lenses|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.99.244801|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=99|issue=24|article-number=244801|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.99.244801|pmid=18233452|arxiv=0705.0320|bibcode=2007PhRvL..99x4801S|s2cid=119171407}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Stancari|first1=G.|last2=Valishev|first2=A.|last3=Annala|first3=G.|last4=Kuznetsov|first4=G.|last5=Shiltsev|first5=V.|last6=Still|first6=D. A.|last7=Vorobiev|first7=L. G.|date=2011-08-17|title=Collimation with Hollow Electron Beams|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.084802|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=107|issue=8|article-number=084802|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.084802|pmid=21929171|arxiv=1105.3256|bibcode=2011PhRvL.107h4802S|s2cid=34630695}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shiltsev|first1=V.|last2=Alexahin|first2=Y.|last3=Burov|first3=A.|last4=Valishev|first4=A.|date=2017-09-27|title=Landau Damping of Beam Instabilities by Electron Lenses|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.134802|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=119|issue=13|article-number=134802|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.134802|pmid=29341724|arxiv=1706.08477|bibcode=2017PhRvL.119m4802S|s2cid=3605871}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title= Electron lenses: Historical overview and outlook|year=2021|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1748-0221/16/03/P03039/meta|language=en|doi=10.1088/1748-0221/16/03/p03039|osti=1779485|s2cid=233837449|last1=Shiltsev|first1=V.|journal=Journal of Instrumentation|volume=16|issue=3|page=03039|bibcode=2021JInst..16P3039S}}</ref>
pioneering [[ground motion]] studies, '''ATL law of ground diffusion''' and data analysis worldwide;<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Shiltsev|first=Vladimir|date=2010-06-07|title=Observations of Random Walk of the Ground in Space and Time|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.104.238501|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=104|issue=23|article-number=238501|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.104.238501|pmid=20867277|arxiv=1202.0027|bibcode=2010PhRvL.104w8501S|s2cid=41072793}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Baklakov|first1=B. A.|last2=Lebedev|first2=P. K.|last3=Parkhomchuk|first3=V. V.|last4=Seryi|first4=A. A.|last5=Sleptsov|first5=A. I.|last6=Shil'Tsev|first6=V. D.|date=1993-10-01|title=Study of seismic vibrations for the VLEPP linear collider|url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1993JTePh..38..894B|journal=Journal of Technical Physics|volume=38|issue=10|pages=894–898|bibcode=1993JTePh..38..894B|issn=1063-7842}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Shiltsev|first=Vladimir|date=2010-09-09|title=Review of observations of ground diffusion in space and in time and fractal model of ground motion|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevSTAB.13.094801|journal=Physical Review Special Topics: Accelerators and Beams|volume=13|issue=9|article-number=094801|doi=10.1103/PhysRevSTAB.13.094801|arxiv=0905.4194|bibcode=2010PhRvS..13i4801S|s2cid=119285303}}</ref>

== Outreach and honors ==
Shiltsev gave many lectures, colloquia and seminars worldwide on the progress and future of modern particle physics, history of particle accelerators, and on Russian polymaths [[Mikhail Lomonosov]] (1711-1765)<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://mediacentral.princeton.edu/id/1_7gbttw70|title= Colloquium|website=www.princeton.edu|access-date=2022-03-20}}</ref>
<ref>{{Cite journal|editor=Vladimir, Shiltsev |date=2012-02-01|title=Mikhail Lomonosov and the dawn of Russian science|journal=Physics Today|volume=65|issue=2|pages=40–46|doi=10.1063/PT.3.1438|bibcode=2012PhT....65b..40S|issn=0031-9228|last1=Shiltsev|first1=Vladimir|doi-access=free}}</ref> and [[Dmitry Mendeleev]] (1834-1907),<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.science20.com/tommaso_dorigo/a_seminar_on_mendeleev-243376|title= A Seminar on Mendeleev|website=www.science20.com|date= 27 August 2014|access-date=2022-03-20}}</ref> and wrote dozens of articles in leading peer-reviewed and pop-sci journals, incl.
